info.title: rIDM Admin API
info.description: Administration API of rIDM. Every operation needs a bearer access token carrying the `urn:ridm:admin` audience; permissions are `ridm:<resource>:<action>`. Errors are RFC 9457 problem documents.

get.summary:
Which master-key generation every encrypted row is under. Spans all
tenants, so global administrators only.

post.summary:
Re-encrypt every row still under an older generation with the current
master key (the new key itself comes from the environment).

get.summary: Who the caller is and what they may do; the admin UI reads this after login.
The permission catalogue and built-in roles (for role editors and docs).
Global administrators see every tenant; tenant-scoped ones see their own.

`?from=&to=&name=&actor_id=&subject_id=&user_id=&cursor=&limit=`; `name`
matches exactly, or as a prefix when it ends with `.` or `*`.
Oldest first, streamed, with the chain hashes so the file can be verified offline.

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: Only mappers bound to this client.

post.summary: Body: `{name, client_id?, config}` where `config` is `{type, ..., include_in}`.

patch.summary: `config` replaces the whole document (mapper types differ too much to merge).

Merge patch over the client's metadata document (every field a `POST`
accepts): send only what changed; `null` clears an optional field or
resets a defaulted one to its type-driven default. `status` may be sent
alongside. Switching to a secret-based auth method mints a secret that is
returned once in `client_secret`.

requestBody.description: JSON merge patch over the client metadata, plus `status`

post.summary:
Issue (replacing any previous one) the RFC 7592 registration access token
so the client's owner can manage its metadata without admin access.

Generate a new secret (first one, or a rotation with a grace window for
the previous secret). The secret is in the response and nowhere else.

put.summary: Create (or return) the user the client acts as under `client_credentials`.

get.summary: Deterministic JSON (sorted keys and collections, natural keys, no secrets).
Flat list with `parent_id`; the UI builds the tree.

patch.summary: `parent_id: null` moves the group to the top level.

put.summary: Every member (and members of descendant groups) gains the role.

post.summary:
`?dry_run=true` returns the plan (creates, updates with field diffs, and
with `prune` deletes). Without it the plan is applied; the report lists
what was applied, any per-item errors, and the secrets of clients and
webhooks the import created (shown once). Applying the same document
again yields an empty plan.

parameters.name: prune
parameters.description: Also delete configuration the document does not mention.

parameters.name: open_only
parameters.description: Only invitations that can still be accepted.

post.summary:
Emails the invitee; roles and groups are granted on acceptance, so they
are checked against the caller's own admin permissions here.
New token and expiry, emailed again; the previous link stops working.

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: Only rules bound to this client.

schema.description:
Lifecycle: pending (published, not yet signing) → active (signing) →
retiring (published for verification only) → revoked (unpublished).

post.summary:
New key with the tenant's default algorithm, active at once; the previous
active key retires with the policy's overlap.
Unpublish now: tokens signed with the key stop verifying.

put.summary:
`{type: "smtp", host, port, username?, password?, from, security?}` or
`{type: "http", url, auth_header?, from}`; an omitted secret keeps the stored one.

post.summary: Put a dead message back in the queue.
Render a stored template or an unsaved draft with sample variables.

put.summary:
Everyone holding `role` gains `child_id`, so the child's permissions
must be within the caller's reach.

get.summary: Users and groups the role is assigned to directly.

put.summary: Admin-catalogue permissions can only be granted by someone who holds them.

post.summary:
Body: every `NewUser` field plus `password` or `temporary_password: true`.
A temporary password is returned exactly once and must be changed at
first login; an explicit password is checked against the tenant policy.

get.summary:
`GET .../users/export?format=json|csv`: every live user, streamed page by
page, without credentials.

post.summary:
`POST .../users/import` with `application/json` (an array of users or
`{"users": [...]}`) or `text/csv` (header row; `attr.<name>` columns become
profile attributes). Rows are processed independently; the report names
every row that failed and why.

requestBody.description: JSON array (or {"users": [...]}) as application/json, or CSV with a header row as text/csv

delete.summary: Soft delete; sessions and trusted devices end at once.

patch.summary:
Partial update: absent = unchanged, `null` clears. `status` covers
enable/disable (`active` / `disabled`); `locked` and `deleted` are set by
the system, use the unlock and delete routes instead.

get.summary: Audit rows where the user is the actor or the subject (`ridm:audit:read`).

delete.summary:
Remove a factor (the user lost the device, say). The password is not a
row here; replace it through `PUT .../password`.

post.summary: Flag the account so the next login demands a new password.
Clear a lockout (failed-attempt counter and `locked` status).

`{name, url, events, enabled?, headers?, max_attempts?}`; the signing
`secret` is in the response and nowhere else.
Requeue and attempt at once; the returned delivery shows the outcome.
Deliver a `webhook.test` event now and report the attempt.

AdminScope.description: How far an administrator's permissions reach.

pattern.description: Anchored regular expression the string form must match.

AuditEvent.description:
One audit row: a domain event as recorded, with its place in the
tenant's hash chain.

payload.description: The event's `kind` document (`type` plus its fields).

seq.description: Position in the chain (per tenant, or the global chain).

subject_id.description: The main entity the event is about (user, client, role, ...), when it has one.

retention_days.description: Days to keep audit rows (0 = forever).

AuthMethods.description: Which first-factor login methods the tenant offers.

CaptchaConfig.description:
CAPTCHA provider configuration. `secret` is only ever handled decrypted
inside the process; the admin API returns it redacted.

verify_url.description: Override the verification endpoint (tests, self-hosted proxies).

CaptchaPolicy.description:
When to demand a CAPTCHA (the provider itself is configured with its
secret in `tenant_provider_settings`).

after_failures.description: Require a challenge after this many failed attempts in a flow (0 = never).

CaptchaView.description: CAPTCHA provider configuration with the secret redacted.

secret_set.description: Always true when configured; the secret itself is never returned.

ClaimMapperRow.description: A stored claim mapper row; `config` is the [`crate::models::ClaimMapper`] document.

ClaimMapperUpdate.description: Partial mapper update; the client scope is immutable.

ClientDoc.description:
A client's metadata document: every field `POST /clients` accepts, plus
`status` and whether it has a service account. Never a secret.

ClientView.description:
Client as returned to administrators: every metadata column, plus the
secrets' ids and validity windows (never the secrets or their hashes).

activate.description:
Publish only (`pending`) unless set, in which case the key starts
signing at once and the previous active key retires with overlap.

oneOf.description: Defaults to the tenant's key policy.

rsa_bits.description: 2048, 3072 or 4096; defaults to the tenant's key policy.

CreatedUser.description: Response to a create or password change that minted a temporary password.

Credential.description:
A user's non-password credential (MFA factors, passkeys, recovery codes),
as listed to administrators and the user: the encrypted material stays
in the row and is never part of this view.

credentials.description: MFA factors, passkeys and recovery codes (metadata only).

allowed_grants.description: Grant types a dynamically registered client may request.

email_domains.description:
`acct:user@<domain>` resources with one of these domains resolve to
this tenant's issuer.

EmailProviderConfig.description: Per-tenant email delivery: SMTP, or an HTTP webhook receiving JSON.

EmailSettingsView.description: Email settings as shown to administrators (no password or auth header).

EmailSource.description: Where email for the tenant goes.

roles.description: Roles assigned to this group itself (ancestors' roles are inherited at runtime).

path.description: Names from the root down; the last element is the group's own name.

ImportRow.description:
One user to import. `roles` and `groups` are names; `password_hash` is a
hash produced elsewhere (argon2, bcrypt, pbkdf2, sha, md5 formats) that
is upgraded transparently at first login; `password` is checked against
the tenant policy.

IpRule.description:
An allow or deny rule for a CIDR, for the whole tenant or one client.
Enforcement is Phase 9.2; this is the configuration.

oneOf.description: Algorithm for new keys created by rotation / on demand.

retire_overlap_hours.description: How long a retired key stays published for verification.

rotation_interval_days.description: Rotate the active key after this many days (0 = never automatically).

KeyStatus.description:
Lifecycle: pending (published, not yet signing) → active (signing) →
retiring (published for verification only) → revoked (unpublished).

ip_max_failures.description: Failures from one IP within the window before it is throttled (0 = off).

max_failures.description: Consecutive failures before a user is temporarily locked (0 = off).

LogEntry.description:
A delivery log entry without the message body (bodies carry links and
codes that must not be readable after the fact).

pending_rows.description: Encrypted rows still under an older generation.

NewClaimMapper.description:
Input for creating a claim mapper: `config` is the mapper document
(`type`, its fields and `include_in`) without the name.

client_id.description: Restrict to one client; absent applies to every client of the tenant.

NewClient.description: Input for creating a client. Missing fields take type-driven defaults.

cidr.description: A network in CIDR notation, or a single address.

identifier.description: Audience value (`aud`) tokens for this API carry; 1-512 characters.

NotificationPolicy.description: Which security notices users receive (email, or SMS when they have no email).

items.description:
One audit row: a domain event as recorded, with its place in the
tenant's hash chain.

payload.description: The event's `kind` document (`type` plus its fields).

seq.description: Position in the chain (per tenant, or the global chain).

subject_id.description: The main entity the event is about (user, client, role, ...), when it has one.

items.description:
Client as returned to administrators: every metadata column, plus the
secrets' ids and validity windows (never the secrets or their hashes).

must_change.description: Force a change at next login (always true for temporary passwords).

notify.description: Email the user that their password changed.

password.description: Absent: generate a temporary password and return it once.

revoke_sessions.description: End the user's sessions so the new password is needed everywhere.

skip_policy.description: Skip the tenant policy and history checks.

check_breached.description: Reject passwords found in breach corpora (Phase 7.5).

history.description:
A new password must differ from the last `history` passwords, counting
the current one (0 = off, 1 = only the current password).

max_age_days.description: Days until a password expires (None = never).

vars.description: The variables the preview was rendered with.

oneOf.description: An unsaved draft to render instead of the stored/built-in template.

locale.description: Locale to resolve when no draft is given (default: tenant default).

vars.description: Extra variables merged over the sample data.

allow_undeclared.description: Accept attributes not declared in the schema (stored verbatim, admin-editable only).

allowed_email_domains.description: Only these email domains may self-register (empty = any).

built_in.description: Seeded by a migration (`urn:ridm:admin`); cannot be changed or deleted.

ResourceServerUpdate.description: Partial resource server update; the identifier is immutable.

RevealView.description: A view plus a secret that is shown exactly once.

built_in.description: Seeded by a migration (the `ridm:*` admin roles); cannot be renamed or deleted.

client_id.description: Client-scoped role when set; realm-wide otherwise.

client.description: Public `client_id` of the client the role belongs to; absent = realm role.

composites.description: Role references: `name` for realm roles, `client_id/name` for client roles.

grace_secs.description:
How long the previous secret keeps working (default 24h, `0` retires
it at once, at most 30 days).

failed.description: Rows that could not be re-encrypted (unknown generation, corrupt blob).

RsaBits.description: RSA modulus size for new RSA keys.

ScopeUpdate.description: Partial scope update; the name is immutable.

resource_server_id.description: Bind to (or, with `null`, unbind from) a resource server.

expires_at.description: `null` while current; set once a rotation retired the secret.

clients.description: Secrets of clients this import created (public `client_id` → secret).

webhooks.description: Signing secrets of webhooks this import created (name → secret).

SigningAlg.description: JWS algorithms rIDM can sign with.

public_jwk.description: Public half as a JWK (`kty`, `kid`, `alg`, `use`, and the key parameters).

SmsProviderConfig.description: SMS delivery through any HTTP gateway.

device_id.description: Trusted device this session was opened from, if any.

events.description: Events rIDM sends messages for; every one has a built-in English template.

overrides.description: Tenant overrides by channel, event and locale.

settings.description: Merge patch applied to the current settings document.

slug.description: Informational: an import applies to the tenant in the URL.

TenantSettings.description:
Per-tenant configuration stored as JSONB. Every field has a default so that
settings written by older versions keep deserializing.

features.description: Feature flags: free-form keys the deployment or its clients consult.

UserDetail.description: The user plus what an admin page shows at a glance.

direct.description: Groups the user is a member of.

effective.description: Direct plus inherited through groups and composites.

broken_at_seq.description: Chain position of the first row whose hash or link does not match.

headers.description: Static headers sent with every delivery.

response_snippet.description: First bytes of the last response body, for diagnostics.

WebhookWithSecret.description: A created or rotated webhook with its secret, shown exactly once.

bearer.description: Access token with the `urn:ridm:admin` audience, issued to a client allowed that audience
